name: API Lifecycle Management & Governance
description: Managing the full API lifecycle from design to deprecation — versioning policies, developer portal experience, API program management, and regulatory compliance. IMPORTANT DISTINCTION: Backend's be_api_design.api_versioning covers implementing URI path versioning (/v1) or Accept header versioning in a single service's codebase (implementation); Backend's be_api_design.openapi_documentation covers generating Swagger UI and writing openapi.yaml files for one service (implementation). API Design's api_lifecycle_governance covers establishing the organization's versioning POLICY (e.g., 'all APIs must support N-1 versions for 12 months'), managing the API catalog/registry across all teams, designing developer portal experiences, running API design review boards, and governing API deprecation/sunset across the entire platform (strategic/architectural decision-making). The backend developer versions their own API; the API designer defines the versioning policy all APIs must follow.

subskills.name: API Versioning Policy & Strategy
subskills.description: Defining organization-wide API versioning policies — versioning strategy selection (URI path vs header vs query param with rationale), N-1 version support window mandates, major vs minor version criteria, and versioning enforcement in CI/CD pipelines.

subskills.name: API Deprecation & Sunset Management
subskills.description: Managing API deprecation lifecycle — Sunset header (RFC 8594) and Deprecation header governance, migration guide requirements, consumer notification timelines, usage-based sunset trigger thresholds, and phased deprecation rollout plans.

subskills.name: API Catalog & Service Discovery
subskills.description: Operating an organization-wide API catalog — API registry platforms (Backstage, Apigee Registry, SwaggerHub), service discovery integration, API taxonomy and tagging standards, ownership metadata requirements, and search/filter capabilities for API consumers.

subskills.name: API Design Review Process & Governance Board
subskills.description: Establishing API design review processes — review board composition and charter, design review checklist criteria, pre-implementation review gates, automated linting (Spectral) as first-pass review, and escalation paths for breaking changes.

subskills.name: API Documentation Standards & Quality
subskills.description: Defining API documentation quality standards — mandatory documentation sections (authentication, errors, rate limits, examples), interactive documentation requirements (try-it-out), code sample language coverage policies, and documentation freshness auditing.

subskills.name: Developer Portal & Experience (DX) Design
subskills.description: Designing developer portal experiences — portal architecture (Backstage, ReadMe, Redocly), onboarding flow optimization, API playground/sandbox integration, getting-started guide standards, and developer journey mapping from registration to first API call.

subskills.name: API Usage Metrics & Analytics
subskills.description: Designing API usage analytics frameworks — key metrics definition (calls/day, unique consumers, error rates, latency percentiles), usage dashboards per API product, consumer adoption tracking, deprecation usage monitoring, and data-driven API investment decisions.

subskills.name: Regulatory Compliance for API Programs
subskills.description: Ensuring API programs meet regulatory requirements — PSD2/Open Banking API compliance, GDPR data minimization in API responses, HIPAA-compliant API data handling, industry-standard API certification programs (FAPI), and audit trail requirements for API access.

subskills.name: API Program Management & Strategy
subskills.description: Managing API-as-a-Product programs — API product roadmapping, internal vs external API strategy, API monetization models (freemium, pay-per-call, subscription tiers), partner API programs, API ecosystem health scorecards, and cross-team API coordination.

subskills.name: API Changelog & Change Communication
subskills.description: Designing API change communication standards — changelog format and tooling (conventional commits for APIs), release notes requirements, breaking change notification channels, developer newsletter governance, and migration guide templates.

mid.description: Manages API deprecation lifecycles with Sunset headers and consumer migration, maintains API catalog registries, participates in design review boards, and improves developer portal onboarding experiences.
